summary: A part of the page in the other theme: a dark header on a light page, a light document preview in a dark app. Everything inside takes the zone's theme, including the menus, popovers, tooltips and dialogs opened from it.
useWhen: one region should stay in one theme whatever the page's — a header that is always dark, a console or log that reads as a terminal
previewing content in the theme it will be seen in — an email or a document that is light even in a dark app

useInstead.when: the whole page should switch theme
useInstead.why: the root carries the page's theme; a zone is the exception inside it, not the switch

useInstead.when: one element should stand out from the page — a callout, a highlighted row
useInstead.why: a surface token from the same theme does that; a zone in the other theme is for a region that belongs to it, not for emphasis

composition.note: `theme` is required: `dark` or `light`. Without `contents` the zone is a block that paints the theme's page surface (`surface/page`) and text colour; with `contents` it draws no box, for wrapping a component that paints its own surface, like a Header, which stays the grid row or sticky element it was. Every themed token is re-declared on the zone, so the components inside need nothing of their own. Menus, popovers, tooltips and dialogs opened from inside it are portalled out of it, so its `overflow` cannot clip them, into a container in the zone's theme. Overlays the zone does not render, such as a navigation Drawer or command palette mounted by the shell, keep the page's theme. Zones nest. `as` picks the element when the zone is a box.
composition.example:
<ThemeZone theme="dark" contents>
  <Header brand={…} end={<NotificationsBell />} />
</ThemeZone>

<ThemeZone theme="light" as="section" aria-label="Email preview">
  <EmailPreview />
</ThemeZone>

dark.use: a region that is dark whatever the page is — a header, a terminal or log

light.use: a region that stays light in a dark app — a preview of a document or email as it will be printed or sent

children.note: drawn in the zone's theme; overlays they open are too

guarantees: every themed token is the zone's, so contrast inside it is the zone theme's: the pairs the contrast gate checks in each theme
text, native controls and scrollbars follow the zone: its text colour and `color-scheme` are set on it
an overlay opened inside it stays reachable when a dialog elsewhere hides the rest of the page
requires: a name for the landmark — a heading inside it, or a label on it — when `as` makes the zone a `section` or `aside`; as a `div`, the default, it needs none
notes: A zone changes colours, not meaning: it adds no role. The zone itself renders on a server, with its theme in the markup.

antiPatterns.why: the attribute alone leaves plain text in the page's colour, native controls in the page's scheme, and every menu or tooltip opened inside it in the page's theme

antiPatterns.dont: a zone around a component that sits in a grid or is sticky, without `contents`
antiPatterns.why: the zone's box becomes the grid cell, and a sticky child can only stick inside it — the Header scrolls away with the page

antiPatterns.dont: zones for emphasis, scattered through a page
antiPatterns.why: a page switching theme region by region reads as broken; one zone is a region with its own job
